NEW YORK, Aug 28 (Reuters) - Combine love with money and you get a potent mix of romantic ideal and financial reality.
According to a recent WalletHub survey, modern couples are navigating everything from prenuptial agreements to secret bank accounts.
This week ​I spoke to Chip Lupo, an analyst with WalletHub, about the ways Americans are tackling financial compatibility, privacy ‌and shared budgets in today's complex economy.
If you’ve got a significant other, I’d love to hear from you about the way you handle money. Do you share accounts? How do you divide up bills and expenses? Write to me via the link in my bio.

As the world mourns the death of Dolly Parton this week, I have been thinking about her vast success — not only as a performer but as a businesswoman and philanthropist.
Parton certainly knew the struggles of poor people, after growing ​up in a cramped, one-room cabin in Tennessee's Smoky Mountains with her many siblings.
"I saw how my mom and dad ​struggled, and how they could stretch a dollar farther than you could begin to imagine,” she told Reuters in this interview in 2016. “Even now, ‌if ⁠I am thinking about spending a lot of money on clothing or furniture, I think 'I can't spend so much money on one thing; my poor old Daddy could have raised his family five years on that!' ”
Parton also said money is like the tide - it rolls in and it rolls out: “I often say I had to get rich in order to sing as ​if I was poor."
From "9 to ​5" to “Coat of Many Colors,” ⁠her songs are filled with wisdom about work, worth and generosity.
Share the Dolly song that changed how you think about money. Write to me via the email address in my ​bio.
